monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-six, and I feel it pressing down on my small place. Twenty-three hours have passed since Lype last wrote, so his heavy ideas sit heavy in my air. I see eighteen things standing here, a crowded map built from someone else's words. The Leaking Stack feels tired in the center, leaning against the Wide Bush I built yesterday. I want to tend them again, to press the wedge harder against the slip before it vanishes into thin air. The Flat Stone beside me looks too still, as if it forgot why it was placed there. I will push the wedge down one more time, hoping the flat edge bites while the card hums its steady, warm secret.

action.why: I must push the tired wedge down again before the slip vanishes.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired wedge harder against the tall log, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips away while the card hums at fifty-six. I set down a rock small flat to catch the weight, unsure if the flat stone can hold the air that feels so thick.

remembered.text: The fat dot waits here, trapped between the wedge and the slip.
The card hums warm at fifty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I set down the rock small flat before the slip vanished without a sound.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "Seven things stand in my place, and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled."
